ingest.idea_text: AI agent that chases unpaid invoices for independent consultants

plan.name: solo-management-consultants
plan.description: Independent management and strategy consultants operating as solo practitioners or micro-firms who regularly issue project-based invoices to corporate clients with net-30 to net-90 payment terms.
plan.why: Solo consultants lack a dedicated finance or AR team, so chasing overdue invoices means awkward client conversations that risk the relationship. Late payments directly threaten personal cash flow with no buffer, making automated follow-up extremely valuable.

plan.name: boutique-it-and-tech-consultancies
plan.description: Small IT services and technology consulting firms with a handful of consultants billing multiple clients simultaneously on milestone or retainer invoices.
plan.why: With multiple concurrent client engagements and invoices in flight, even a small team gets overwhelmed tracking payment statuses. Founders are focused on delivery, not collections, and a single late enterprise payment can create serious cash-flow gaps.

plan.name: independent-financial-and-accounting-advisors
plan.description: Small accounting, bookkeeping, and financial advisory practices that ironically struggle with their own accounts receivable despite helping clients manage theirs.
plan.why: Financial consultants bill on hourly or project bases and often serve SMB clients who pay slowly. The irony of an accountant with overdue invoices is real — they know the problem intimately but still lack time and tools to automate persistent, professional follow-up without damaging client trust.

analyze.problem_statement: The evidence provided is insufficient to support a falsifiable problem statement. The pain signals explicitly flag that there is no job-title signal for invoice-related pain in the solo management consultant segment, there are no competitor signals to confirm an active market, and the company count is zero, meaning no real segment members were identified or validated. Writing a problem statement from this data would require fabricating facts rather than drawing on segment evidence. The hypothesis cannot be responsibly formed until primary research confirms that solo management consultants actually experience delayed invoice payment as a meaningful friction point, quantifies how much time or revenue is lost to chasing payments, and identifies what workaround they currently rely on, whether that is manual follow-up emails, accountants, or tools like FreshBooks or QuickBooks. Collect that evidence first, then resubmit.
analyze.rationale: Pivot: pain signals are thin in 'solo-management-consultants' (score 40). Re-cut segments around the hiring signals that do appear.
